svg.title: What crosses a chain boundary between estates, as what, and by which standard

g.text: eip155:<chain>:<address>; one hex on two chains is two accounts until a signed binding joins them
the card lists her accounts by chain, each with a proof that account signed; round trip per chain
one home registry per typed root; addr records by chain; per-chain reverse claim; proof elsewhere
re-issued on the chain where it acts; the EIP-712 domain carries the chain id and the manager
one read on the grant’s chain; the live-grant root is refreshed and a stale root is a refusal
the membership root on public ground; a Merkle presentation reveals one leaf, nothing else
anchored where the act ran; the vault record names the chain; a mirrored anchor is evidence only
a treasury invokes a bridge adapter under a mandate redeemable only on the destination chain
the indexer reads each chain; every fact carries its chain; still only what the chain can prove
the estate’s governance address is its id on public ground; the charter hash sits beside its roots
a rotation or recovery at the home reaches each satellite by its own custody action; proofs re-signed

svg.text: Two things never cross: a grant and the read of its revocation. Everything else crosses as a reference, a signed list, a proof, an anchor, a transfer or a ceremony.
Bridges and messaging gateways are adapters in sibling repositories. Ring 0 ships the fields they carry: a chain on every reference, a chain and an anchor on every receipt, a root per estate.

g.text: A message from another chain is evidence that something happened there. It is never a mandate here.
